questions.prompt: Which reference parameter type refuses to bind to `const Widget cw;` while accepting `Widget{}`?
options: const Widget&
Widget&&
const Widget&&
Widget&
questions.explanation: Widget&& binds only non-const rvalues (xvalues and prvalues like Widget{}), rejecting lvalues such as cw. const Widget& and const Widget&& accept const rvalues (though const Widget& also accepts cw), while Widget& rejects both.

questions.prompt: What value does `r` observe after `d = 9.5;` runs in this snippet?
options: 3, because r bound to a temporary int{3} created by converting d rather than aliasing d
9, because r aliases d and truncates its updated value on read
Compilation error: const int& cannot bind to a double
Undefined behavior due to strict aliasing between int and double
questions.explanation: Because int and double are not reference-related, binding const int& to double d implicitly converts d into a fresh temporary int{3} whose lifetime is extended to r. Subsequent writes to d never affect that hidden temporary.

questions.prompt: In which snippet does `r` (or `h.ref`) remain valid rather than dangling immediately after the semicolon?
options: const int& r = id(10);
Holder h(10);
const int& r = make_pair().first;
std::string_view sv = std::string("abc");
questions.explanation: Binding a reference directly to a non-static data member subobject of a temporary (make_pair().first) extends the entire temporary Pair object's lifetime to r. Passing through id(), storing via a non-aggregate constructor Holder, or constructing std::string_view stops lifetime extension.

questions.prompt: In C++17 and C++20 (before C++23 P2718R0), what happens in `for (int x : make_box().get_vec())` when `get_vec()` returns `const std::vector<int>&`?
options: Well-defined in all C++ versions because range-for extends every temporary in the header
Well-defined only if int x is changed to const auto& x
Compile error in C++17/C++20
Undefined behavior in C++17/C++20 because auto&& __range binds to get_vec()'s return reference, letting the Box temporary destruct before the loop starts
questions.explanation: In C++11 through C++20, range-for initializes auto&& __range = make_box().get_vec();. Because get_vec() is a member function call, __range does not extend the Box temporary, which is destroyed at the semicolon before iteration begins. C++23 P2718R0 fixed this in [stmt.ranged].

questions.prompt: What do `std::reference_converts_from_temporary_v<const std::string&, std::string>` and `std::reference_converts_from_temporary_v<const std::string&, std::string&>` evaluate to in C++23?
options: false and false, because both have the same underlying type std::string
true and false, because std::string (unqualified) models a prvalue that materializes a temporary, whereas std::string& is an lvalue that binds directly
false and true
true and true
questions.explanation: In <type_traits> ([meta.unary.prop]), the second template argument U models an expression of type declval<U>(). When U is std::string (non-reference), declval<std::string>() is an rvalue, so binding const std::string& creates/materializes a temporary (true). When U is std::string&, declval<std::string&>() is an lvalue and binds directly (false).

questions.prompt: When an aggregate struct `struct Agg { const std::string& s; };` is aggregate-initialized via `Agg a{"hello"};`, what is the lifetime of the materialized `std::string` temporary?
questions.code:
struct Agg { const std::string& s; };
Agg a{"hello"};
options: It is destroyed at the semicolon of Agg a{"hello"};, leaving a.s dangling
It is extended to match the lifetime of a (the enclosing aggregate object)
It lives in static storage until program exit
Aggregate initialization of a reference member from a string literal is ill-formed
questions.explanation: Under [class.temporary]/6.1, a temporary bound to a reference element of an aggregate via aggregate initialization has its lifetime extended to match the lifetime of the aggregate object a itself—unlike a user-declared constructor's mem-initializer, which does not extend lifetime.
